C: A1 the part of the face that sticks out above the mouth, through which you breathe and smell
› specialized food & drink the particular smell of a wine
› the front of a vehicle, especially an aircraft
（車輛的）前端突出部；（尤指飛機）機頭

I usually + adv/prep: › [ I usually + adv/prep ] informal to look around or search in order to discover something, especially something that other people do not want you to find
窺探，打探（尤指他人不欲公開的事）；搜尋

I or T, + adv/prep: › [ I or T,  + adv/prep ] to (make a vehicle) move forwards slowly and carefully

example: a large/long/pointed nose
大／長／尖鼻子
I had a sore throat and a runny nose (= liquid coming out of the nose).
我喉嚨痛，還流鼻涕。
See also
nasal
a wine praised for its smoky nose
因其煙熏味而備受稱道的葡萄酒
The symbol was painted on each side of the plane's nose.
飛機機頭兩側都繪有這標誌。
There were some reporters nosing about/around.
有些記者在四處打探新聞。
The police came in and started nosing into drawers and looking through papers.
警方到來後開始搜查抽屜，翻檢文件。
The car nosed out of the side street, its driver peering anxiously around.
司機一邊緊張地四下張望，一邊小心翼翼地把車駛出小路。
He carefully nosed his lorry into the small space.
他小心翼翼地把大卡車開進這個狹窄的空間。

NONE: › the front part of a spacecraft, aircraft, or missile (= flying weapon)
› used to describe the way someone behaves when they think they are better than other people and do not want to speak to them

example: She walked past me with her nose in the air.
她旁若無人地從我身邊走過。

NONE: › to have an operation to change the shape of your nose
› to discover something by searching carefully

example: He soon nosed out the details of the accident by talking to people and making some phone calls.
和人們隨意閒聊並打了幾通電話之後，他很快就摸清了事故的細節。

NONE: › a small piece of jewellery connected to a short, thin piece of metal that passes through the side of the nose
鼻釘（鑲在鼻子一側的小枚珠寶）

example: She wondered if she should take out her nose stud for the job interview.
她不知道是否應該為了參加面試而摘下鼻釘。
The cars were parked nose to tail down the street.
汽車一輛緊接著一輛地停在街道上。

NONE: › the wheel at the front of an aircraft
› a bag for holding food that is hung around a horse's head
› an occasion when blood comes out of a person's nose

example: She gets/has a lot of nosebleeds.
她經常流鼻血。

NONE: › having a nose of the type mentioned

example: sharp/snub/hook-nosed
尖鼻子／塌鼻子／鷹鉤鼻的
a blunt-nosed missile
鈍頭導彈

NONE: › a fast and sudden fall to the ground with the front pointing down
› a sudden fast fall in prices, value, etc.
› to suddenly fall to the ground with the front pointing down
› to suddenly fall in value, quickly and by a large amount

example: The plane roared overhead and went into a nosedive.
飛機在頭頂發出轟鳴，然後向下俯衝。
There was alarm in the markets when the dollar took a nosedive.
美元暴跌時，各種市場一片恐慌。
Spectators in the crowd watched in horror as the plane nosedived.
觀眾驚恐地看著飛機俯衝下來。
House prices nosedived without warning.
事先沒有任何預警房價突然暴跌。

NONE: › UK old-fashioned slang food or a meal

U: › [ U ] US informal a small amount of food eaten between meals or as a meal

example: They serve good nosh in the cafeteria.
餐廳的食物很不錯。

我10點半的時候吃了些零食，這樣午餐就不會吃太多。
US We asked the waiter for something to nosh on while we waited for a table.

We had some good nosh-ups on holiday.
節日期間，我們吃了幾頓豐盛的大餐。

NONE: C2 feeling happy and also slightly sad when you think about things that happened in the past

example: Talking about our old family holidays has made me feel all nostalgic.

NONE: C2 either of the two openings in the nose through which air moves when you breathe

example: The horses came to a halt, steam streaming from their nostrils.
